newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Freeport Indonesia says copper costs to fall.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Freeport Indonesia says copper costs to fall.

text.p: Mining group PT Freeport Indonesia Co said on Wednesday that it expected copper production costs at its Irian Jaya operation to fall to less than US$0.20 a pound for calendar 1996 from US$0.236 last year.

"In 1996 we would expect our cash production costs ... after taking into account our gold and silver credits, to go well below US$0.20 per pound," executive vice-president and chief financial officer Stephen Jones told a resources conference.
Freeport Indonesia is an affiliate of Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc.
Jones said Freeport's Irian Jaya operation would become the second lowest cost copper producer in the world.
Freeport Indonesia, one of the world's biggest copper and gold miners, has a copper and gold mine and mill at Tembagapura in the Irian Jaya highlands.
New Orleans-based Freeport McMoRan owns 82 percent of PT Freeport Indonesia. The Indonesian government and PT Indocopper Investama each own nine percent.
